text.p: Following are some of the major events to have occurred on June 25 in history:
1080 - A council of bishops at Brixen declared Pope Gregory to be deposed and Archbishop Guibert as antipope Clement III.
1580 - The Book of Concord, a collection of doctrinal standards of the Lutheran Church, was first published.
1788 - Virginia became the 10th state of the United States.
1867 - The first barbed wire was patented by Lucien B. Smith of Ohio.
1870 - Queen Isabella of Spain abdicated in favour of Alfonso XII.
1870 - Irish nationalist Erskine Childers born. He joined the Irish Republican Army in 1921 and was captured by the Free State authorities and executed. His son became Irish President in 1973.

1876 - At the Battle of the Little Big Horn, Sioux Indians led by Chief Crazy Horse routed the U.S. 7th Cavalry led by Colonel Custer. Custer died along with his company of 264 men in what was known as "Custer's Last Stand".
1900 - Earl Louis Mountbatten, British naval commander and statesman, born. He became first sea lord and last viceroy of India.
1903 - George Orwell was born as Eric Arthur Blair in Bengal. He became famous as an essayist and novelist whose works included "Animal Farm" and "Nineteen Eighty Four".
1910 - The first performance of "The Firebird", a ballet by Igor Stravinsky, took place in Paris.
1938 - Gaelic scholar Douglas Hyde was inaugurated as the first president of the Irish Republic.
1940 - In World War Two, hostilities in France formally ended after the French signed an armistice with Germany the previous week.
1942 - Major General Dwight Eisenhower was appointed commander of U.S. forces in Europe; on the same day, General Sir Claude Auchinleck became commander of the British Eighth Army in North Africa.
1950 - North Korea invaded South Korea, heralding the beginning of the Korean War.
1951 - The first regular commercial colour TV transmissions were inaugurated by CBS from New York.
1953 - The notorious British murderer of Ten Rillington Place, John Christie, was sentenced to death for killing six women.
1959 - Eamon De Valera became President of Ireland at the age of 76.
1968 - British comedian Tony Hancock was found dead in a Sydney hotel room after committing suicide.
1973 - Erskine Childers Jr. became president of Ireland after the retirement of Eamon de Valera.
1975 - Mozambique became independent and Samora Machel was sworn in as president after 477 years of Portuguese rule.
1976 - Johnny Mercer, U.S. popular song composer and actor, died. He also wrote the lyrics for a number of award winning songs including "Moon River".
1982 - Alexander Haig resigned as U.S. Secretary of State and George Schultz took over.
1984 - Lord Carrington of Britain succeeded Joseph Luns as NATO Secretary-General.
1991 - The last Soviet troops stationed in Czechoslovakia left the country, 23 years after the Warsaw Pact invasion.
1991 - Croatia and Slovenia declared independence from Yugoslavia, plunging the federation into a violent breakup.
1993 - Kim Campbell took office as Canada's first woman prime minister.
1993 - Jacques Attali, head of the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development, resigned saying press attacks had undermined the bank's work.
1994 - Japanese Prime Minister Tsutomu Hata resigned along with his minority government rather than face a no-confidence vote in parliament.
1996 - A bomb blast tore through a Saudi Arabian military complex housing foreigners, killing 19 Americans and injuring nearly 400.
